speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and have they changed in appearance or size since they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the exposure history and the description of the lesions, are the papules raised, firm, and pearly white with central umbilication, and have you noticed any signs of secondary bacterial infection like crusting or pus?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of umbilicated, pearly papules is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
